_meta.note: Hand-authored international catalog so fixture mode still answers for people outside the regional worlds. Shaped like Qloo Insights entities plus a `_syn` block used for scoring and stripped before serving. Entity ids are fake. Not Qloo data.

properties.short_description: 'La Vie en rose' and 'Non, je ne regrette rien'; the voice of Paris.
Madrid-born balladeer of 'La vida sigue igual' and 'Hey!', one of the best-selling Latin artists ever.
'La Bohème', 'She'; the Armenian-French chansonnier who sang for seven decades.
Greek singer in the famous glasses, with hits in a dozen languages from the 1960s on.
'Blowin' in the Wind', 'Like a Rolling Stone'; the songwriter of the 1960s.
The Queen of Soul: 'Respect', '(You Make Me Feel Like) A Natural Woman'.
Cairo-born star of French chanson and disco: 'Bambino', 'Gigi l'amoroso'.
'Merci, Chérie' won Eurovision in 1966; 'Griechischer Wein', 'Mit 66 Jahren': the Austrian at the white piano, all over German-speaking Europe.
'Ganz Paris träumt von der Liebe', 'Malagueña': the polyglot star of 1950s Europe who sang in a dozen languages.
'Mon credo', 'Acropolis adieu', 'Santa Maria de la mer': the voice from Avignon that Germany, Spain and Japan adopted.
'Forever and Ever', 'Goodbye My Love Goodbye': the Greek in the kaftan who sold Europe its summer of 1973.
'Rivers of Babylon', 'Daddy Cool', 'Rasputin': the disco act from Germany that every European wedding played.
'Massachusetts', 'How Deep Is Your Love', 'Stayin' Alive': from the ballads of the sixties to the disco floor of 1977.

properties.description: Bogart, Bergman and 'As Time Goes By' in wartime Morocco.
Audrey Hepburn's runaway princess tours Rome on a Vespa with Gregory Peck.
Gene Kelly, Debbie Reynolds and Donald O'Connor in the greatest Hollywood musical.
Fellini's Rome of nightclubs and the Trevi Fountain, with Marcello Mastroianni and Anita Ekberg.
Jacques Demy's sung-through romance in candy colors, with Catherine Deneuve and Michel Legrand's score.
Anthony Quinn dances the sirtaki on a Cretan beach; Theodorakis's theme went around the world.
Saint-Germain café since 1887, once the haunt of Sartre and de Beauvoir.
Roast suckling pig from a wood oven since 1725; the world's oldest restaurant by Guinness's reckoning.
Rome's grand café on Via Condotti since 1760, red velvet and marble tables.
Gustave Eiffel's 1889 iron tower on the Champ de Mars.
Rome's baroque fountain of 1762; toss a coin over your shoulder to return.
Madrid's central square, the clock that rings in the New Year and the Bear and the Strawberry Tree.
Madrid's great park: rowing boats on the lake and the Crystal Palace.
The city of light: the Seine, the cafés, the boulevards.
The Eternal City: the Colosseum, the Vatican and gelato on the Spanish Steps.
Gondolas, St Mark's Square and the Lido.
Trams, fado and the Tagus.
Waikiki Beach, Diamond Head and the honeymoon flights of the jet age.
Nice, Cannes and Saint-Tropez: the French Riviera of Bardot and the film festival.
David Lean's Russia, Omar Sharif and Julie Christie, and 'Lara's Theme' on the balalaika.
Audrey Hepburn's Eliza and Rex Harrison's Higgins, the Ascot scene and 'I Could Have Danced All Night'.
Dustin Hoffman, Mrs Robinson and Simon and Garfunkel; the plastics line.
The shark, the beach, the two notes; the summer nobody went in the water.
John Travolta's white suit and the Bee Gees on the Brooklyn dance floor.
Travolta and Olivia Newton-John at Rydell High; 'Summer Nights' and 'You're the One That I Want'.
Marilyn Monroe, Tony Curtis and Jack Lemmon on the train to Florida; nobody's perfect.
Charlton Heston and the chariot race, eleven Oscars and every Easter television schedule since.
The Jets and the Sharks, Natalie Wood's Maria, 'Tonight' and 'America' on the fire escapes.
Romy Schneider as the young empress; the Christmas film of German-speaking Europe for seventy years.
Judy Garland's Dorothy, the yellow brick road and 'Over the Rainbow'.
Vivien Leigh's Scarlett and Clark Gable's Rhett; frankly, my dear.
One Saturday night a year since 1956: the songs, the costumes and the scoreboard, from Lugano to everywhere.
The Cartwrights of the Ponderosa, Hoss and Little Joe, the burning map; fourteen seasons shown around the world.
Horst Tappert's Munich inspector and Harry's car; Germany's detective, dubbed into every language in Europe.
Kermit, Miss Piggy, the two old men in the balcony and a guest star every week.
J.R. Ewing, Southfork and the question of who shot him; the serial the whole world watched.
Saturday night with Frank Elstner and then Thomas Gottschalk: the bets, the sofa and the stars.
The chases, the saxophone and the little old man; sold to a hundred countries.
The Ring, the Prater wheel, the Sachertorte and the Opera Ball.
The canals, the bicycles and the tulips at Keukenhof.
The lemon houses, the lake steamers and the first family holiday abroad.
Winter sun under Mount Teide, the black beaches and the package hotels of the Playa de las Américas.
The umbrellas in rows on the Adriatic, the pensione and the evening passeggiata.
Chalets, cowbells and the first ski trip; Innsbruck, Zermatt and Garmisch.
Palma's cathedral, the coves and the beaches of the Bay of Pollença.

properties.short_description: 'Jolene', '9 to 5': the Tennessee songwriter whose records sold everywhere.
